questions.prompt: Which of these take room in the context window of a coding agent, and which do not?
questions.explain: Instructions, files read, tool output and the conversation itself all count. Files that were never read and your terminal scrollback do not.

items.text: The text of a file the agent just read
items.misconception: Every file it reads is added to the window.

items.text: The output of a command it ran
items.misconception: Tool output is added, whether or not you see it.

items.text: Your instructions file, loaded at session start
items.misconception: Instructions load before you type and use space every session.

items.text: A file in the project that was never opened
items.misconception: Unread files are not in the window until the agent reads them.

items.text: A terminal command you ran before the session started
items.misconception: Only what reaches the session counts.

questions.prompt: What does Anthropic's documentation say happens as the amount of context grows?
questions.explain: The docs say accuracy and recall degrade as tokens grow, and they name it context rot. They give no threshold.

options.text: Accuracy and recall can degrade (context rot)
Quality usually rises steadily until the window is full
options.misconception: The docs describe accuracy and recall degrading as context grows.

options.text: Nothing changes, since the model weighs all tokens equally
options.misconception: The docs describe degradation, so equal weighing is a risky assumption.

questions.prompt: What does the KV cache hold while a model writes a long reply?
questions.explain: The model stores numbers (keys and values) computed from each earlier token and reuses them, so it does not redo that work at every step. The store grows with the window. The prompt cache is a separate, provider-side feature.

options.text: Numbers computed from earlier tokens, reused for each new token
A saved copy of your prompt that the provider bills at a lower rate
options.misconception: That describes the prompt cache. The KV cache belongs to the model.

options.text: The files in your project, kept in memory between sessions
options.misconception: Project files enter the window only when the agent reads them.

questions.prompt: You told the agent a rule once early in a long session, and after compaction it is ignored. What is the most likely reason?
questions.explain: The docs say detailed instructions from early in the conversation may be lost when history is summarised. Rules that must last belong in the instructions file.

options.text: The summary dropped it, since it only lived in chat
The model refuses rules it has been given only once
options.misconception: The cause is the window: the text is no longer in it.

options.text: The instructions file was deleted by the compaction
options.misconception: The project-root instructions file is supplied again after compaction.

questions.prompt: A request to an agent during a long session. Which line is the problem for the context window?
questions.explain: Printing a whole large table puts all of it into the window. Ask for a count, the head, or a script output.

lines.text: Count the rows in variants.tsv with a command and show the number
lines.why: A count is a tiny output.

lines.text: Run cat on variants.tsv and read it all
Show me the first ten lines and the column names
lines.why: The head is small and shows the shape.

lines.text: Write a short script that summarises the filters and run that
lines.why: Only the summary enters the window.
